verses.zh: 耶路撒冷王亚多尼・洗德听见约书亚夺了艾城，尽行毁灭，怎样待耶利哥和耶利哥的王，也照样待艾城和艾城的王，又听见基遍的居民与以色列人立了和约，住在他们中间，
verses.en: Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem,[NOTE:1] heard how Joshua captured Ai and annihilated it and its king as he did Jericho[NOTE:2] and its king.[NOTE:3] He also heard how[NOTE:4] the people of Gibeon made peace with Israel and lived among them.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
Heb “as he had done to Jericho and to its king, so he did to Ai and to its king.”
Heb “and how.”

verses.zh: 就甚惧怕；因为基遍是一座大城，如都城一般，比艾城更大，并且城内的人都是勇士。
verses.en: All Jerusalem was terrified[NOTE:1] because Gibeon was a large city, like one of the royal cities. It was larger than Ai, and all its men were warriors.
notes: This statement is subordinated to v. 1 in the Hebrew text, which reads literally, “When Adoni-Zedek…they feared greatly.” The subject of the plural verb at the beginning of v. 2 is probably the residents of Jerusalem.

verses.zh: 所以耶路撒冷王亚多尼・洗德打发人去见希伯仑王何咸、耶末王毗兰、拉吉王雅非亚，和伊矶伦王底璧，说：
verses.en: So King Adoni-Zedek of Jerusalem sent this message to King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon:

verses.zh: 「求你们上来帮助我，我们好攻打基遍，因为他们与约书亚和以色列人立了和约。」
verses.en: “Come to my aid[NOTE:1] so we can attack Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and the Israelites.”
notes: Heb “Come up to me and help me.”

verses.zh: 于是五个亚摩利王，就是耶路撒冷王、希伯仑王、耶末王、拉吉王、伊矶伦王，大家聚集，率领他们的众军上去，对着基遍安营，攻打基遍。
verses.en: So the five Amorite kings (the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon) and all their troops gathered together and advanced. They deployed their troops and fought against Gibeon.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they camped against Gibeon and fought against it.”

verses.zh: 基遍人就打发人往吉甲的营中去见约书亚，说：「你不要袖手不顾你的仆人，求你速速上来拯救我们，帮助我们，因为住山地亚摩利人的诸王都聚集攻击我们。」
verses.en: The men of Gibeon sent this message to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal, “Do not abandon[NOTE:1] your subjects![NOTE:2] Come up here quickly and rescue us! Help us! For all the Amorite kings living in the hill country are attacking us.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “do not let your hand drop from us.”
Heb “your servants!”
Heb “have gathered against us.”

verses.zh: 于是约书亚和他一切兵丁，并大能的勇士，都从吉甲上去。
verses.en: So Joshua and his whole army, including the bravest warriors, marched up from Gilgal.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the brave warriors.”

verses.zh: 耶和华对约书亚说：「不要怕他们；因为我已将他们交在你手里，他们无一人能在你面前站立得住。」
verses.en: The Lord told Joshua, “Don’t be afraid of them, for I am handing them over to you.[NOTE:1] Not one of them can resist you.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I have given them into your hand.” The verbal form is a perfect of certitude, emphasizing the certainty of the action.
Heb “and not a man [or “one”] of them will stand before you.”

verses.zh: 约书亚就终夜从吉甲上去，猛然临到他们那里。
verses.en: Joshua attacked them by surprise after marching all night from Gilgal.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Joshua came upon them suddenly, all the night he went up from Gilgal.”

verses.zh: 耶和华使他们在以色列人面前溃乱。约书亚在基遍大大地杀败他们，追赶他们，在伯・和仑的上坡路击杀他们，直到亚西加和玛基大。
verses.en: The Lord routed[NOTE:1] them before Israel. Israel[NOTE:2] thoroughly defeated them[NOTE:3] at Gibeon. They chased them up the road to the pass[NOTE:4] of Beth Horon and struck them down all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.
notes: Or “caused to panic.”

Heb “he.” The referent is probably Israel (mentioned at the end of the previous sentence in the verse; cf. NIV, NRSV), but it is also possible that the Lord should be understood as the referent (cf. NASB “and He slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon”), or even Joshua (cf. NEB “and Joshua defeated them utterly in Gibeon”).
Heb “struck them down with a great striking down.”
Or “ascent.”

verses.zh: 他们在以色列人面前逃跑，正在伯・和仑下坡的时候，耶和华从天上降大冰雹（原文是石头）在他们身上，直降到亚西加，打死他们。被冰雹打死的，比以色列人用刀杀死的还多。
verses.en: As they fled from Israel on the slope leading down from[NOTE:1] Beth Horon, the Lord threw down on them large hailstones from the sky,[NOTE:2] all the way to Azekah. They died—in fact, more died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with the sword.
notes: Heb “on the descent of.”
Or “heaven” (also in v. 13). The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.

verses.zh: 当耶和华将亚摩利人交付以色列人的日子，约书亚就祷告耶和华，在以色列人眼前说：日头啊，你要停在基遍；月亮啊，你要止在亚雅仑谷。
verses.en: The day the Lord delivered the Amorites over to the Israelites, Joshua prayed to the Lord before Israel:[NOTE:1] “O sun, stand still over Gibeon; O moon, over the Valley of Aijalon!”
notes: Heb “Then Joshua spoke to the Lord in the day the Lord placed the Amorites before the sons of Israel and he said in the eyes of Israel.” It is uncertain whether the phrase “before the sons of Israel” modifies the verb “placed” (as in the present translation, “delivered the Amorites over to the Israelites”) or the verb “spoke” (“Joshua spoke to the Lord before the sons of Israel in the day the Lord delivered over the Amorites”).

verses.zh: 于是日头停留，月亮止住，直等国民向敌人报仇。这事岂不是写在雅煞珥书上吗？日头在天当中停住，不急速下落，约有一日之久。
verses.en: The sun stood still and the moon stood motionless while the nation took vengeance on its enemies. The event is recorded in the Scroll of the Upright One.[NOTE:1] The sun stood motionless in the middle of the sky and did not set for about a full day.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Scroll of the Upright One was apparently an ancient Israelite collection of songs and prayers (see also 2 Sam 1:18), but it has not been preserved. tn Heb “Is it not written down in the Scroll of the Upright One?” Many modern translations render this as “the Book of Jashar.” Yashar (יָשָׁר) means “Upright One.”

Heb “and did not hurry to set [for] about a full day.”sn The nature of the event described here is debated. Various options have been suggested, including (1) the earth stopped rotating, (2) the light of the sun somehow shone longer than normal, (3) the light of the sun was blocked by an eclipse, (4) the position of the sun and moon in the sky was interpreted as an omen, or (5) the language is figurative and metaphorical, describing the battle in poetic terms. For a good discussion of these options, see D. M. Howard, Jr., Joshua (NAC), 241-49.

verses.zh: 在这日以前，这日以后，耶和华听人的祷告，没有像这日的，是因耶和华为以色列争战。
verses.en: There has not been a day like it before or since. The Lord listened to a human being, for the Lord fought for Israel!

verses.zh: 约书亚和以色列众人回到吉甲的营中。
verses.en: Then Joshua and all Israel returned to the camp at Gilgal.

verses.zh: 那五王逃跑，藏在玛基大洞里。
verses.en: The five Amorite kings[NOTE:1] ran away and hid in the cave at Makkedah.
notes: Heb “these five kings.”

verses.zh: 有人告诉约书亚说：「那五王已经找到了，都藏在玛基大洞里。」
verses.en: Joshua was told, “The five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah.”

verses.zh: 约书亚说：「你们把几块大石头滚到洞口，派人看守，
verses.en: Joshua said, “Roll large stones over the mouth of the cave and post guards in front of it.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and appoint by it men to guard them.”

verses.zh: 你们却不可耽延，要追赶你们的仇敌，击杀他们尽后边的人，不容他们进自己的城邑，因为耶和华－你们的　神已经把他们交在你们手里。」
verses.en: But don’t you delay! Chase your enemies and catch them.[NOTE:1] Don’t allow them to retreat to[NOTE:2] their cities, for the Lord your God is handing them over to you.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “But [as for] you, don’t stand still, chase after your enemies and attack them from the rear.”
Or “enter into.”
Heb “has given them into your hand.” The verbal form is a perfect of certitude, emphasizing the certainty of the action.

verses.zh: 约书亚和以色列人大大杀败他们，直到将他们灭尽；其中剩下的人都进了坚固的城。
verses.en: Joshua and the Israelites almost totally wiped them out, but some survivors did escape to the fortified cities.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “When Joshua and the sons of Israel finished defeating them with a very great defeat until they were destroyed (now the survivors escaped to the fortified cities).” In the Hebrew text the initial temporal clause (“when Joshua…finished”) is subordinated to v. 21 (“the whole army returned”).

verses.zh: 众百姓就安然回玛基大营中，到约书亚那里。没有一人敢向以色列人饶舌。
verses.en: Then the whole army safely returned to Joshua at the camp in Makkedah.[NOTE:1] No one[NOTE:2] dared threaten the Israelites.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “all the people returned to the camp, to Joshua [at] Makkedah [in] peace.”
Heb “No man.” The lamed (ל) prefixed to אִישׁ (ʾish, “man”) is probably dittographic (note the immediately preceding יִשְׂרָאֵל [yisraʾel] which ends in lamed, ל); cf. the LXX.

Heb “no man sharpened [or perhaps, “pointed”] his tongue against the sons of Israel.” Cf. NEB “not a man of the Israelites suffered so much as a scratch on his tongue,” which understands “sharpened” as “scratched” (referring to a minor wound). Most modern translations understand the Hebrew expression “sharpened his tongue” figuratively for opposition or threats against the Israelites.

verses.zh: 约书亚说：「打开洞口，将那五王从洞里带出来，领到我面前。」
verses.en: Joshua said, “Open the cave’s mouth and bring the five kings[NOTE:1] out of the cave to me.”
notes: Heb “these five kings.”

verses.zh: 众人就这样行，将那五王，就是耶路撒冷王、希伯仑王、耶末王、拉吉王、伊矶伦王，从洞里带出来，领到约书亚面前。
verses.en: They did as ordered;[NOTE:1] they brought the five kings[NOTE:2] out of the cave to him—the kings of Jerusalem,[NOTE:3] Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
notes: Heb “they did so.”
Heb “these five kings.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 带出那五王到约书亚面前的时候，约书亚就召了以色列众人来，对那些和他同去的军长说：「你们近前来，把脚踏在这些王的颈项上。」他们就近前来，把脚踏在这些王的颈项上。
verses.en: When they brought the kings out to Joshua, he[NOTE:1] summoned all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the troops who accompanied him, “Come here[NOTE:2] and put your feet on the necks of these kings.” So they came up[NOTE:3] and put their feet on their necks.
notes: Heb “Joshua.” The translation has replaced the proper name with the pronoun (“he”) because a repetition of the proper name here would be redundant according to English style.
Or “Draw near.”
Or “drew near.”

verses.zh: 约书亚对他们说：「你们不要惧怕，也不要惊惶。应当刚强壮胆，因为耶和华必这样待你们所要攻打的一切仇敌。」
verses.en: Then Joshua said to them, “Don’t be afraid and don’t panic![NOTE:1] Be strong and brave, for the Lord will do the same thing to all your enemies you fight.”
notes: Or perhaps “and don’t get discouraged!”

verses.zh: 随后约书亚将这五王杀死，挂在五棵树上。他们就在树上直挂到晚上。
verses.en: Then Joshua executed them[NOTE:1] and hung them on five trees. They were left hanging on the trees until evening.
notes: Heb “struck them down and killed them.”

verses.zh: 日头要落的时候，约书亚一吩咐，人就把尸首从树上取下来，丢在他们藏过的洞里，把几块大石头放在洞口，直存到今日。
verses.en: At sunset Joshua ordered his men to take them down from the trees.[NOTE:1] They threw them into the cave where they had hidden and piled large stones over the mouth of the cave. (They remain to this very day.)[NOTE:2]
notes: For the legal background of the removal of the corpses before sundown, see Deut 21:22-23.
Heb “to this very day.” The words “They remain” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 当日，约书亚夺了玛基大，用刀击杀城中的人和王；将其中一切人口尽行杀灭，没有留下一个。他待玛基大王，像从前待耶利哥王一样。
verses.en: That day Joshua captured Makkedah and put the sword to it and its king. He annihilated everyone who lived in it; he left no survivors. He did to its king what he had done to the king of Jericho.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

verses.zh: 约书亚和以色列众人从玛基大往立拿去，攻打立拿。
verses.en: Joshua and all Israel marched from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against it.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Libnah.” Repetition of the proper name here would be redundant according to English style, so the pronoun (“it”) has been employed in the translation.

verses.zh: 耶和华将立拿和立拿的王也交在以色列人手里。约书亚攻打这城，用刀击杀了城中的一切人口，没有留下一个。他待立拿王，像从前待耶利哥王一样。
verses.en: The Lord handed it and its king over to Israel, and Israel[NOTE:1] put the sword to all who lived there; they[NOTE:2] left no survivors. They did to its king what they had done to the king of Jericho.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he”; the implied subject may be Israel, or Joshua (as the commanding general of the army).
Heb “he”; the implied subject may be Israel, or Joshua (as the commanding general of the army). So also for “They did to its king” and “they had done.”
For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

verses.zh: 约书亚和以色列众人从立拿往拉吉去，对着拉吉安营，攻打这城。
verses.en: Joshua and all Israel marched from Libnah to Lachish. He deployed his troops[NOTE:1] and fought against it.
notes: Heb “encamped against it.”

verses.zh: 耶和华将拉吉交在以色列人的手里。第二天约书亚就夺了拉吉，用刀击杀了城中的一切人口，是照他向立拿一切所行的。
verses.en: The Lord handed Lachish over to Israel, and they[NOTE:1] captured it on the second day. They put the sword to all who lived there, just as they had done to Libnah.
notes: Heb “he”; the implied subject may be Israel, or Joshua (as the commanding general of the army).

verses.zh: 那时基色王荷兰上来帮助拉吉，约书亚就把他和他的民都击杀了，没有留下一个。
verses.en: Then King Horam of Gezer came up to help Lachish, but Joshua struck him down, as well as his army,[NOTE:1] until no survivors remained.
notes: Heb “people.”

verses.zh: 约书亚和以色列众人从拉吉往伊矶伦去，对着伊矶伦安营，攻打这城。
verses.en: Joshua and all Israel marched from Lachish to Eglon. They deployed troops[NOTE:1] and fought against it.
notes: Heb “they encamped against it.”

verses.zh: 当日就夺了城，用刀击杀了城中的人。那日，约书亚将城中的一切人口尽行杀灭，是照他向拉吉一切所行的。
verses.en: That day they captured it and put the sword to all who lived there. That day they[NOTE:1] annihilated it just as they had done to Lachish.
notes: Heb “he”; the implied subject may be Israel, or Joshua (as the commanding general of the army). So also for “they had done to Lachish.”

verses.zh: 约书亚和以色列众人从伊矶伦上希伯仑去，攻打这城，
verses.en: Joshua and all Israel marched up from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it.

verses.zh: 就夺了希伯仑和属希伯仑的诸城邑，用刀将城中的人与王，并那些城邑中的人口，都击杀了，没有留下一个，是照他向伊矶伦所行的，把城中的一切人口尽行杀灭。
verses.en: They captured it and put the sword to its king, all its surrounding cities, and all who lived in it; they[NOTE:1] left no survivors. As they had done at Eglon, they annihilated it and all who lived there.
notes: Heb “he”; the implied subject may be Israel, or Joshua (as the commanding general of the army). So also for “they had done” and “they annihilated.”

verses.zh: 约书亚和以色列众人回到底璧，攻打这城，
verses.en: Joshua and all Israel turned to Debir and fought against it.

verses.zh: 就夺了底璧和属底璧的城邑，又擒获底璧的王，用刀将这些城中的人口尽行杀灭，没有留下一个。他待底璧和底璧王，像从前待希伯仑和立拿与立拿王一样。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] captured it, its king, and all its surrounding cities and put the sword to them. They annihilated everyone who lived there; they[NOTE:2] left no survivors. They did to Debir and its king what they had done to Libnah and its king and to Hebron.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “He”; the implied subject may be Israel, or Joshua (as the commanding general of the army).
Heb “he”; the implied subject may be Israel, or Joshua (as the commanding general of the army). So also for “They did to Debir” and “they had done to Libnah.”
Heb “as he did to Hebron, so he did to Debir and its king, and as he did to Libnah and its king.” The clauses have been rearranged in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 这样，约书亚击杀全地的人，就是山地、南地、高原、山坡的人，和那些地的诸王，没有留下一个。将凡有气息的尽行杀灭，正如耶和华―以色列的　神所吩咐的。
verses.en: Joshua defeated the whole land, including the hill country, the Negev,[NOTE:1] the foothills,[NOTE:2] the slopes,[NOTE:3] and all their kings. He left no survivors. He annihilated everything that breathed, just as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
notes: The Negev is an area of central southern Judah, south of the hill country and west of the rift valley. As a geographic feature it is a depression extending south to the Gulf of Aqabah, but the biblical reference is probably to the northern portion of the region.
The foothills (שְׁפֵלָה, shephelah) are the transition region from the hill country to the Mediterranean coastal plains.
In contrast to the foothills on the western side of the hill country, the slopes are on the eastern side leading down to the rift valley of the Dead Sea and Jordan river.

verses.zh: 约书亚从加低斯・巴尼亚攻击到迦萨，又攻击歌珊全地，直到基遍。
verses.en: Joshua conquered the area between Kadesh Barnea and Gaza and the whole region of Goshen, all the way to Gibeon.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and Joshua struck them down, from Kadesh Barnea even to Gaza, and all the land of Goshen, even to Gibeon.”

verses.zh: 约书亚一时杀败了这些王，并夺了他们的地，因为耶和华―以色列的　神为以色列争战。
verses.en: Joshua captured in one campaign[NOTE:1] all these kings and their lands, for the Lord God of Israel fought for Israel.
notes: Heb “at one time.”

verses.zh: 于是约书亚和以色列众人回到吉甲的营中。
verses.en: Then Joshua and all Israel returned to the camp at Gilgal.
